problem_type: Agent composer mixed work mode, approval/spend policy, Skill, and prompt-library controls in one resident menu
symptom: Users could not predict where to change the Agent work posture or load a Skill because the mode popover contained four unrelated groups, while the creation surface also repeated storyboard-plan output in a card below the editor.
direct_cause: ProjectAgentResidentShell rendered work mode, approval policy, spend policy, Skill rows, and prompt entry as one menu, and CreationWorkspace mounted StoryboardPlanCard as a second storyboard entry point.
class_root: The resident composer had no enforced one-function-one-home boundary: capability selection, execution policy, and navigation were allowed to accumulate in a single always-visible control path.
affected_population: All Agent surfaces using the resident composer
Users selecting a Skill or prompt preset
Creation users opening a generated storyboard plan
Keyboard and screen-reader users relying on stable composer order
entry_points: Resident composer buttons on creation, storyboard, generation, and preview surfaces
internal_only_reason: This remediation enforces Nomi's approved §1.5 one-function-one-home and 2026-09-05 Agent UI decision; no third-party behavior determines the invariant.
invariants: The composer DOM order is attachments, model, Skill, spacer, work mode, send/stop.
The mode popover contains only the work-mode segmented control; approval and spend remain readable request state in the store with a TODO for the B-segment介入槽.
Prompt-library selection is reachable from the Skill capability menu without a second resident composer button.
A completed storyboard plan has one Creation navigation home: its document-list row opens storyboard directly; Agent shows a compact receipt affordance.
Running feedback is visible around the prompt field until the active turn ends and reduces to a static token outline under prefers-reduced-motion.
generality_proof: All four Agent surfaces mount the same ProjectAgentResidentShell, so the single composer implementation governs every caller. Both storyboard navigation paths converge on useWorkbenchStore workspace mode and storyboard selection; removing the middle-column card eliminates the duplicate creation entry while the Agent receipt reuses the existing task/artifact receipt interaction shape.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own composer order, capability/menu ownership, mode-only popover, running feedback, and storyboard receipt projection.
Make the canonical storyboard resource row select its design and enter storyboard workspace in one action.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The same resident shell is portaled into each workspace surface and is the only production composer implementation.
The card is removed; storyboard plans remain owned by StoryboardWorkspace and the document-list row/Agent receipt provide the approved entries.
It edits a generation node's media parameters, not the resident Agent capability or execution-policy menu.

recurrence.reason: Any new resident capability or policy can recreate the same mixed-menu problem, and every creation plan could regain a duplicate navigation card unless shared ownership is explicit.
same_class_scan: rg ProjectAgentResidentShell across WorkbenchShell confirmed one shared resident implementation mounted at four surfaces.
rg StoryboardPlanCard confirmed CreationWorkspace was its only production mount; the file is removed with the duplicate entry.
rg setActiveStoryboardId and setWorkspaceMode confirmed DocumentListSidebar and StoryboardWorkspace are the shared storyboard navigation boundary.

prevention.invariant: Only capability selection lives under Skill, only work posture lives under Mode, and execution policy fields are never rendered as composer menu rows.
prevention.failure_mode: A future policy addition has no composer entry until the B-segment介入槽 owns it; the existing store values continue to travel with every request.
prevention.strategy: Keep one resident shell as the sole composer owner, derive the visible order from its JSX, and route storyboard opening through the shared workspace store boundary.

legacy_paths.rationale: The middle-column summary card was the duplicate storyboard navigation path and is deleted in the same change as the canonical row/receipt flow.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The change uses existing React, Tabler, Nomi design primitives, and browser media-query behavior; no third-party runtime controls the invariant.

migration: No persisted schema changes. Existing approval/spend store values remain readable and continue through run requests; existing storyboard designs remain addressable through the document list and StoryboardWorkspace.
residual_risks: The B-segment介入槽 that will expose approval and spend choices is intentionally deferred and remains a visible TODO in the resident shell.
The conformance geometry contract may require updated composer anchors because the approved order removes the prompt button and adds Skill.
